abstract: Non-invasive interrogation of difficult-to-sample tissues remains a central challenge in human health. Here, we identify and characterize cardiomyocyte-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs; "cardiovesicles") as a liquid interface to the myocardium. Integrating induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, genetic models, and multi-omics, we identify two cardiomyocyte-enriched surface markers (POPDC2 and CHRNE), enabling antibody-based cardiovesicle immunocapture from human plasma. Cardiovesicles are enriched for cardiomyocyte transcripts, exhibiting disease-specific transcriptional signatures in heart failure and myocardial infarction. Paired human myocardial tissue-plasma analyses demonstrate cardiac enrichment (versus bulk EVs) and concordance with myocardial single-nucleus transcriptional profiles. In patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass, cardiovesicles capture rapid, dynamic transcriptional changes that parallel cardiomyocyte (not fibroblast, endothelial, and myeloid) responses to ischemic stress. Functional genomics implicates cardiovesicle transcripts in cardiomyocyte cell-specific cardiovascular disease liability in large human populations. Cardiovesicles may capture dynamic cardiomyocyte states in humans that reflect genetic disease liability, supporting an EV-based approach to non-invasive liquid biopsy of the myocardium.
